 Visit To The Dump Leads To Unexpected Reunion Between Woman And Her Missing Dog
 “I felt such an overwhelming surge of emotion!”
 By Stephen Messenger Published on Nov 18, 2026 at 5:39 PM For the past five years, Adrián Contreras, founder of Helping the Dogs of the Trelew Landfill , has helped care for dogs living in and around a vast open-air dump in Trelew, Argentina. He and his partner bring the dogs food and water and arrange sterilization and medical care when they can.
 “A unique challenge in our work is that many of the dogs living at the landfill are feral,” Contreras told The Dodo. “These animals were either born or raised with virtually no positive human contact; they live in packs and, due to fear and distrust, often won’t let anyone get close to them.”
 But during one recent visit, Contreras noticed a dog who wasn’t like the others.
 Ayuda Perritos del Basural Trelew Contreras usually drives to the dump, but when his van broke down, he rode his bike there to check on the dogs. That’s when he spotted a newcomer — a small, fluffy dog who stood out from the rest.
 “The feral dogs who live there are mixed breeds,” Contreras said. “It’s quite rare to see a poodle, or any other specific breed, at the landfill.”
 Contreras gently tried to coax the small dog toward him, but the pup, afraid, ran the other way.
 On his bike, Contreras followed.
 Ayuda Perritos del Basural Trelew “After following [the dog] for several kilometers, I waited for him to tire out and stop running, all the while keeping him in sight,” Contreras said. “Eventually, he came across a pile of rubble, weeds and trash, where he crouched down.”
 Ayuda Perritos del Basural Trelew Contreras had livestreamed videos of his pursuit of the dog on Helping the Dogs of the Trelew Landfill’s Facebook page .
 “Almost immediately, someone reached out — they had been searching for their dog, Toby, that matched his description,” Contreras said. “We asked for a photograph of the missing dog. When we saw the picture, we couldn’t believe it. It was him! We had found Toby!”
 Toby, who lives with his family in town, had been missing for nearly a week.
 Ayuda Perritos del Basural Trelew To keep Toby from bolting off again, Contreras and a worker at the dump placed him in a makeshift crate. His worried mom, meanwhile, caught the first cab she could find to meet them at the spot.
 When she arrived, Contreras captured touching video of their reunion:
 Ayuda Perritos del Basural Trelew “I felt such an overwhelming surge of emotion!” Contreras said. “Witnessing that reunion — seeing Toby wag his tail, happy and grateful in his owner’s arms — was truly moving.”
 Ayuda Perritos del Basural Trelew It’s not often that a dog found at the landfill ends up in a loving home. But Contreras, through his work with Helping the Dogs of the Trelew Landfill, hopes for more happy endings.
 “I would love for the world to learn not just about Toby and his heartwarming reunion, but also about the reality faced by so many animals surviving daily in an open-air dump, and the immense effort required to help them,” Contreras said. “Our greatest hope is that, one day, it will no longer be necessary to rescue dogs from a dump — because that would mean we’ve succeeded in changing this reality.”
